summary: Burst-credit misallocation after subaccount reparenting causing opaque 429s for mixed real-time and batch ingest
description:
Issue summary: After a planned reparent operation that moved two high-volume subaccounts under a new org umbrella, DataPulse began seeing opaque 429s affecting both realtime chat streams and nightly bulk-embedding jobs. This appears correlated with the reparent window (2026-03-11 03:00-03:10 UTC).

Impact: Multiple DataPulse services had a significant portion of requests rejected with 429 for ~40 minutes, causing downstream backlog for their batch pipeline and user-facing latency spikes for realtime features. Customer reports 18% failure rate on embed backfills and sporadic 429 for low-rate chat sessions.

Timeline:
- 2026-03-11 02:58 UTC: orchestration triggered subaccount reparenting (internal operation id orch-2026-311-77).
- 2026-03-11 03:04 UTC: first customer report of 429 surge.
- 2026-03-11 03:25 UTC: engineering rollback of a non-critical flag; 429s persist.
- 2026-03-11 03:45 UTC: support engaged; initial triage points to quota accounting.

Environment: prod-us-east (dedicated pool: dp-dedicated-03), mixed HTTP2 websocket and REST ingest.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Start concurrent embed backfill (1000 concurrent workers) for subaccount A.
2) Simultaneously run realtime chat load (50 concurrent websockets) on subaccount B (now under same parent).
3) Observe intermittent 429 responses with X-RateLimit headers showing token window near zero.

Observed behavior: 429s show as "rate limit exceeded" but total tenant quota in console still shows available burst credits. Token window counters on several ingress nodes show inconsistent attribution where short-lived auth tickets were counted against the pre-reparent subaccount mapping.

Relevant logs / metrics (samples):
- ingress-proxy logs (03:03:59 UTC): "token_bucket_check: key=subacct-A:worker-77, counted=1200, window=60s, remaining=0"
- rate-limiter debug (03:04:19 UTC): "burst_pool_lookup: parent_org=org-X, subaccount_id=subacct-B -> burst_pool_id=pending-reassign-9001"
- billing/credits service (03:05:02 UTC): "credit_balance: org-X total=1.2M, subacct-A=800k, subacct-B=400k"

Notes: X-RateLimit headers were present but sometimes omitted on websocket handshake rejects; customer SDK did not surface consistent retry-after values.

Customer asks: immediate mitigation to avoid lost requests, and explain what caused burst-credit accounting to be out-of-sync after reparenting.

Desired outcome: restore stable request acceptance for both realtime and batch traffic while preserving correct burst allocation; implement reconciliation to avoid recurrence.
comments: 2026-03-11 03:50 UTC - Support (Ava Kline): Thanks for the report, DataPulse. We're triaging with SRE. Can you confirm whether you performed any API key rotation as part of the reparent? Also please attach a sample request id and websocket connection id when you see a 429.

2026-03-11 03:58 UTC - Customer (Elena M., DataPulse): No key rotation. Sample request id: req-20260311-37e1. Websocket accept id: ws-44b2. We saw the first 429s immediately after the new parent mapping appeared in console.

2026-03-11 04:10 UTC - SRE (Noah Patel): Initial hypothesis: reparent operation temporarily created a 'pending' burst_pool mapping (burst_pool_id=pending-reassign-9001) and the ingress nodes used the old token->subaccount mapping for some short-lived tokens; this led to double accounting against a single burst pool causing local window exhaustion. Collecting rate-limiter counters and ingress node token->subaccount cache TTLs now.

2026-03-11 05:22 UTC - SRE (Noah Patel): Collected counters show several ingress nodes with stale mapping TTLs ~120s during reparent; one worker shows 2x counting for ephemeral tokens. Opening INT ticket for orchestration. Marking workaround: temporarily pin subaccounts to isolated burst pools for DataPulse to stop cross-subaccount bleed.

2026-03-12 09:15 UTC - Support (Ava Kline): Workaround applied at 2026-03-12 07:45 UTC: assigned isolated burst pools (dp-burst-iso-121). Customer confirms error rate dropped to <1% for realtime and backfill resumed. We flagged for permanent fix. Customer asked for timeline.

2026-03-13 14:02 UTC - SRE (Maya Fernandez): We've reproduced a race condition in the orchestration reparent path where burst_pool assignments are written asynchronously to the credit-index service; ingress lookup can hit an intermediate state. Patch proposed (PR linked) to make the reparent operation atomic w.r.t burst_pool mapping. Scheduling canary rollout to dp-dedicated-03.

2026-03-14 11:30 UTC - Support (Ava Kline): Customer notified. Planning coordinated release windows and final reconciliation job. Pending: post-deploy verification and a follow-up report to DataPulse.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: token-to-subaccount cache TTL during reparent allowed short-lived tokens to be attributed to old subaccount while burst pool moved -> local double-counting.
Hypothesis 2: credit-reconciliation batch lagged; UI showed correct totals but runtime credit_index didn't reflect reparent until after some ingest nodes performed heavy counting.
Evidence: consistent ingress cache TTLs ~120s; rate-limiter logs show 'pending-reassign' pool id used transiently; after isolating burst pools, 429s stopped.
Action items taken: 1) isolated burst pools for DataPulse (workaround), 2) enabled verbose ingress mapping logs for the next 24h, 3) created INT follow-up for orchestration atomicity (INT-220).
Next checks: run reconciliation job to backfill any misapplied token counts; add test in reparent integration test to simulate concurrent short-lived token usage.
resolution: Workaround applied: isolated burst pools assigned to affected subaccounts (dp-burst-iso-121). This reduced 429s to <1% and allowed the customer's backfill to complete. Root cause: race in orchestration reparent path that left transient 'pending' mappings visible to ingress nodes, causing misattributed counting against a single burst pool. Permanent fix in progress (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/1823) to make burst_pool assignment atomic and to emit coordinated cache invalidation events. Follow-ups: schedule reconciliation job to correct any miscounted tokens, add integration test, and deploy canary to dp-dedicated-03 next maintenance window.
